coverage_note: Read the whole transcript. Many stretches are English/meta discussion and were not counted as Arabic errors; chat-only cleanups were used only as context. No echo-candidates file was provided inline. I omitted clear pronunciation/root-letter slips such as سجر/فجر per S4 unless the exchange also showed a wrong lexical choice.

rows.why: Amal recast the adjective as feminine; the next turn confirms he was talking about his fiancée, so sick needed عيانة.
خطيبتي is feminine and Amal again supplied عيانة, also typing 5atibti shwai 3ayaane.
rows.english: My fiancée is a little sick.

rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: He explicitly said he did not know the word and Amal supplied كح/كحة, saying she says كحة.

rows.medi_said: بنقلق؟ بنقلق worried. No worried would be past tense. No we are worrying. Yeah we are worrying. Is it بنقلق؟
rows.amal_said: No, you can use the adjective. Or I worry. Do you wanna say I worry?
rows.why: He used the verb بنقلق for the state 'we are worried'; Amal said to use the adjective, and he fixed it to قلقانين.

rows.amal_said: Men not. You're worried from. You're worried about. You're worried from.
rows.why: Amal explicitly rejected لـ and gave من for قلقانين من نار; her chat confirms min naar.

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for? I don't know how to say this right.
rows.why: He said he did not know how to say the phrase, and Amal supplied ديرت بالي.
rows.english: I took care / I was taking care.

rows.why: Amal supplied the possessive ending in بالي and the required preposition على before خطيبتي.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.why: Amal explicitly named that بدير بالي takes على, so the preposition was missing.
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.

rows.why: After خلينا / let's, Amal supplied the bare present نعمل rather than the past عملنا.
He said he forgot the word for sky and Amal supplied سما, later typing sama = sky.
He gave the singular غيم for clouds; Amal prompted that it was one item, and he fixed it to غيوم.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطل-- no، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟
rows.why: He understood بتطلع as 'look/watch', and Amal explicitly contrasted بتتطلع على with الشمس بتطلع 'the sun goes up'.
rows.english: When does the sun rise / go up?

rows.medi_said: does it has to do with Azan? No. ... Is it Azan?
rows.amal_said: أذان؟ No. أذان is the call to prayer. [تضحك] فجر.
rows.why: He guessed Azan for the time the sun comes up; Amal said أذان is the call to prayer and supplied فجر.
Amal explicitly rejected the extra لو and gave the phrase as غير.

rows.medi_said: غير الشمس و غيوم شو في.
rows.why: Amal recast with غير شمس; غير in front does not take el-.
rows.english: Other than the sun and clouds, what is there?

rows.chat: el-sma billail fi el-2amar u njoom, u 3itme

rows.chat: el-sma billail fi el-2amar u njoom, u 3itme

Amal prompted the pointer rule, and he added the object ending ها: بشوفها اليوم.

rows.medi_said: since is لسـ-- لسا, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. ... Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: He used لسا/لا for since; Amal rejected them, said لا is until, and supplied من.
For 'it rains' Amal supplied the feminine/impersonal form بتمطر, not بمطر.

rows.medi_said: غير من because it's comparative, right?
rows.why: Amal corrected the fixed preposition for غير to عن; chat confirms 8eir 3an.

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... صح. آخر مرة. The last time.

Amal prompted that مرة is feminine, and he changed كان to كانت.
rows.english: The last time was three years ago.

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين أو الماضيات would be for the last three years. Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.chat: aa5er marra tallajat kaanat 2abel talat sneen
rows.why: Amal explicitly said الماضيين would mean 'the last three years' and that ago is قبل before the number/time unit.

rows.medi_said: قبل ثلاث. قبل always goes before. قبل ثلاث سنان.
rows.why: Amal asked what سنان means and then contrasted it with سنين; chat notes snaan = teeth and sneen = years.

rows.chat: aa5er marra tallajat kaanat 2abel talat sneen

rows.amal_said: رملة sand. ... التراب. تراب is dirt or soil.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made. ... الشوارع الإدام في أمريكا حجر.
rows.proposed_rule: To describe what something is made of as a material, say the thing is the material directly, not 3amal/ma3: الشوارع الإدام في أمريكا حجر.
rows.why: Amal rejected 'made with stone' and said to use حجر directly because 'made of is different than made'.
rows.english: The old streets in America are stone.

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.chat: the second stone was my favorite
rows.why: For 'the second stone' Amal corrected the order to تاني حجر; حجر تاني means another stone.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.why: Amal taught that 'my favorite' in this predicate use is المفضل عندي, not a pronoun ending on مفضل.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: Amal said المفضل is an adjective and put it after the noun: الحجر المفضل / حجري المفضل.

rows.medi_said: Yeah، okay. So الـ حجري الـ مفضل.
rows.why: Amal explicitly removed the first ال because the possessive ending in حجري already makes it definite; the adjective stays المفضل.

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
rows.why: Amal explained that المفضل is a definite adjective following الدرس and modeled هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.

rows.medi_said: So it's not المفضل إلي, it would be المفضل عندي, right?
rows.why: In the favorite construction, Amal had just modeled عندي and confirmed his correction away from إلي.
rows.english: the favorite to me / my favorite

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.

rows.english: His favorite book is not here.
